channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: EUR/GBP trades in a tight range ahead of UK jobs data
item.description: EUR/GBP is holding a narrow band around the mid-0.8500s with little conviction in either direction. At the time of writing, the cross is close to flat on the day.

item.title: The US Dollar Index cannot rally with Washington on the offer
item.description: The Dollar Index trades near 99.50, roughly a tenth of a percent lower, having opened directly on its 200-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and failed there inside the first minutes, with a session low just above 99.25 taking out the August range.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average lets refiners price the war
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 53,550 on Monday, down close to 200 points and roughly 1,200 beneath the record printed on August 5, on the day the 60-day negotiating window that was meant to end the war over the Strait of Hormuz lapses with nothing agreed to replace it.

item.title: WTI Oil climbs above $82 as Washington-Tehran standoff reignites supply concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil advances on Monday and trades around $82.10 at the time of writing, up 0.68% on the day. Oil prices remain supported by the deadlock between the United States (US) and Iran, which keeps concerns about Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz elevated.

item.title: British Pound edges higher as traders await UK jobs and CPI data
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) registers modest gains of 0.14% on Monday against the US Dollar (USD) as investors digest softer-than-expected US inflation data and brace for the release of crucial UK jobs and inflation data. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3552 after hitting a three-month high of 1.3571.

item.title: Gold strengthens above $4,400 as Fed rate-hike expectations fade
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its intraday advance on Monday, supported by fading expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at its September meeting, while the US Dollar (USD) remains on the back foot. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,425, up 1.11% on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles despite rising bond yields and BoJ hike bets
item.description: USD/JPY rebounds on Monday after coming under selling pressure earlier in the day, as the Japanese Yen (JPY) struggles to gain traction despite a weaker US Dollar (USD). At the time of writing, the pair trades around 159.25, recovering from an intraday low of 158.85.

item.title: Silver accelerates above $66 as Fed expectations shift
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its advance on Monday and trades around $66.30 at the time of writing, up 2.47% on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs to two-month highs amid a soft US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD extended its recovery on Monday, pushing to fresh 10-week highs and holding near the 0.7100 zone. At the time of writing, the pair is 0.40% up for the day, driven almost entirely by a broadly weak US Dollar (USD) rather than anything positive out of Australia.

item.title: British Pound: Bullish bias with data risk ahead against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note British Pound (GBP) is underperforming core European peers but has still reached a three‑month high against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: China: High-tech sectors cushion broader slowdown – ING
item.description: According to ING’s Lynn Song, Chinese industrial production growth slowed more than expected in July but remains relatively resilient compared with other domestic indicators.

item.title: US Dollar: Faces renewed downside risk – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that the US Dollar (USD) has weakened against the Euro (EUR) as markets steadily scale back expectations for further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening relative to other G10 central banks.

item.title: Gold: Investors extend longs but hedge risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that money managers sharply increased long Gold exposure as modest inflation, soft United States (US) employment data and expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will not hike rates this year weigh on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro: Bullish momentum eyes mid‑1.17s against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the Euro (EUR) is firming as Eurozone economic resilience and narrowing yield spreads versus the US support EUR/USD.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Inflation steady near target – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Abbey Xu and Nathan Janzen note that Canadian inflation rose to 3% year-over-year in July, mainly on higher energy costs, while underlying measures like CPI-trim and CPI-median stayed near the 2% target.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy doubts weigh on Yen – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that weak Japanese Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data and rising JGB yields are undermining confidence in the Bank of Japan’s ability to sustain a stronger Yen.

item.title: Canadian Dollar firms after hotter-than-expected inflation data
item.description: USD/CAD falls to its lowest level since June 3 on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) stays under pressure, while hotter-than-expected Canadian inflation data provided additional support to the Canadian Dollar (CAD). At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.3852.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles against Euro as inflation accelerates to 3%
item.description: EUR/CAD edges higher on Monday, trading around 1.6070 at the time of writing, up 0.11% on the day. The pair maintains a positive bias despite a stronger-than-expected acceleration in Canadian inflation, which provides some support to the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: China: Fiscal support to offset weak demand – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding note that China’s July real activity data showed weaker momentum, with estimated monthly Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth dropping below 4.3% year-on-year.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar hits two-month high as US Dollar weakness offsets softer China data
item.description: NZD/USD extends its advance on Monday and trades around 0.5915 at the time of writing, up 0.37% on the day.

item.title: Taiwan: Strong double-digit GDP expansion to persist – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Ma Tieying revises Taiwan’s 2026 GDP growth forecast up to 11.6% from 9.4% and 2027 to 5.6% from 4.5%, noting that growth will exceed 10% and mark the strongest pace in more than three decades.

item.title: Breaking: Canada headline CPI rose by 3% YoY in July
item.description: Canada’s inflation picked up pace in July, with the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 3% from a year earlier, above market expectations and up from the 2.8% increase recorded in June. On a monthly basis, prices rose 0.5%.

item.title: United States: Sideways growth and sticky inflation – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir expect US output growth to move sideways in 2025 as the lingering Oil shock and Iran conflict create stagflationary risks, keeping the Fed on hold.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Bulls press toward 1.3600 as uptrend strengthens
item.description: GBP/USD edges higher on Monday as fading expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike drag the US Dollar (USD) lower and lift the British Pound (GBP) to its highest level since May 12.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Further gains seen versus Euro - Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that the Norwegian Krone (NOK) is the strongest G10 currency across multiple horizons, supported by Oil prices, above-target inflation and a hawkish Norges Bank.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI move tightens liquidity – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that India’s bonds sold off after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) unexpectedly advanced closure of its special Dollar deposit window to end-August.

item.title: Japan: BoJ path questioned on weak demand – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economists Reo Sakida and Jin Kenzaki say Japan’s 2Q GDP data were weaker than expected, with consumption and capex both disappointing.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls eye 185.00 resistance area
item.description: The Euro (EUR) crawls higher for the third consecutive day on Monday, against a weak Yen (JPY), weighed down by downbeat Japanese Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures.

item.title: Economists agree: Fed to leave interest rates unchanged this year – Reuters poll
item.description: A large majority of economists expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to keep interest rates unchanged in September and for the rest of this year, according to a Reuters poll conducted between August 12 and 17.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk near 160 highlighted – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee of DBS Group Research notes that markets still focus on Japan’s struggle to support the Japanese Yen, while underplaying broader USD implications.
